title: sustainability notes: inference energy & low-carbon serving ideas
content:
Quick brain-dump / reading roundup about energy measurements for model inference and pragmatic low-carbon serving approaches. Intended as a personal scratchpad before drafting a short doc for infra/product.

Why I care (context):
- Redwood sells economic predictability for inference. Unit cost usually focuses on $/token, but energy and carbon are both reputational + regulatory risks for customers (finance, health, gov).
- If we can expose energy-per-token and optimize for low-carbon regions, that's a differentiator for enterprise deals and sustainability commitments.

Papers/blogs skimmed (notes):
- Strubell et al. (2019) "Energy and Policy Considerations for Deep Learning in NLP" — shows training carbon footprint; key takeaway: training dominates, but inference at scale (100s of millions reqs/day) becomes nontrivial. Think about cumulative effects and tail latency tradeoffs.
- CarbonTracker (website) — useful toolkit for per-job estimation (GPU type, runtime, utilization). Could adapt a lightweight estimator for per-request inference energy by combining kernel-level power draw with token time.
- Several cloud provider posts on "low-carbon regions" and scheduling to match renewable availability. There's also work on grid-aware routing.

Back-of-envelope numbers (very rough):
- Example: A T4-like GPU at 80% utilization maybe draws ~150W for inference steady-state (guess). If per-request latency average is 50ms and per-request utilizes 1/16th of GPU during beam, then energy per request ~150W * 0.05s / 16 ≈ 0.47 Wh (0.0017 MJ). Multiply by 100M requests => ~47 kWh/day? (these are order-of-magnitude placeholders — need measurement.)
- The point: small per-request energy accumulates; batching and packing matter a lot.

Operational levers (what Redwood could do):
- Measure first: implement a micro-benchmark harness that records GPU power draw (nvidia-smi/powercap) during representative RT workloads and correlates to tokens. Build a small E/U estimator service.
- Expose energy-per-token and estimated CO2e per-route in Console for enterprise customers. Allow customers to set routing policies like "prefer-low-carbon".
- Region-aware scheduling: route non-latency-sensitive batch work to regions with higher renewables or lower grid carbon intensity.
- Time-of-day batching: for asynchronous jobs (embeddings, bulk rerank) schedule during greener windows if customers opt-in.
- Instance selection: surface energy profiles for model variants (quantized vs fp16 vs fully sharded) and recommend low-energy variants when quality trade-offs are acceptable.
- Autoscaling with carbon-aware objectives: include energy/cost/latency multi-objective in autoscaler (hard to do, but possible as an opt-in policy).

Ideas for experiments to run (short-term):
1) "Per-token power sweep" — run a controlled synthetic prompt load across a small fleet of GPU types we support (A10, A100s, H100?) capturing power, temp, util, latency, tokens generated. Output: regression model mapping tokens->Wh per token for each model+hardware combo.
2) "Batching energy audit" — with same average throughput, compare many small requests vs curated batching at different batch sizes; measure marginal energy per token and tail-latency impact.
3) "Region carbon routing pilot" — pilot routing for internal non-prod workload to two regions with known grid differences; measure differences and quantifiable CO2 reduction.

Questions and open risks:
- Measurement fidelity: can we trust nvidia-smi polling at low timescales? Need kernel-level or rack PDUs for accurate numbers. Also PUE varies a lot by datacenter.
- Attribution: If we route to low-carbon region but use more compute (longer paths, replication), net effect could be worse. Need to model whole-system.
- Customer expectations: Do customers want to trade latency/cost for lower carbon? Need UX for opt-in, defaults for enterprise contracts.
- Compliance/regulation: Some customers may need proofs/audit logs of carbon accounting; we'd need standardized methods.

Notes to self (write-up plan):
- Draft a 1-page "Energy & Inference: why Redwood cares" for infra/product leads. Include two slides: measurement plan + low-effort wins (quantization recommendation, scheduling noncritical batch work).
- Follow-ups: sync with Solutions Eng to see early enterprise asks; triage feature as "Console beta".

Quick checklist (next actions):
- [ ] Prototype per-token estimator (script + small fleet run) — assign to Leo.
- [ ] Add GH issue to runtime to surface GPU power metrics to metrics pipeline (#082?) — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/482
- [ ] Short internal demo for product PMs showing how energy metrics could look in Console (mock screenshots)
- [ ] Survey 3 customers (AE + CSM) for interest in low-carbon routing feature

Voice / style notes for final doc: keep it pragmatic, focus on measurable wins we can ship in 3 months. Avoid moralizing — pitch as both cost + sustainability win.

Random fragments / thoughts:
- Could sell an "ESG mode" for enterprise that defaults to quantized models and low-carbon region routing within SLA.
- Add energy metrics to cost breakdowns (show $ + Wh + CO2e) for transparency.

References to copy into final doc:

- CarbonTracker: https://carbontracker.org/
